assertions.name: dashboard_m_p_error_equals_triangulation_residual
assertions.source: q_0 is Newton-pinned so that m_p_pred == m_e * MASS_RATIO_P_E identically; the scored row must therefore reproduce leg 1 exactly. It does, to within the dashboard's own 4-significant-figure serialization of err_ppb (which is the limiting term here, not the physics). The m_p row measures registry inconsistency and nothing else.

assertions.name: proton_triple_inconsistent_beyond_printed_granularity
assertions.source: Indicator (1 = residual exceeds 10x the last printed digit of m_p; see leg1_residual_in_printed_units for the magnitude). Within one CODATA adjustment the triple is a single correlated fit output, so a same-edition triple agrees to its last printed digit. The residual is ~126x that unit, which rounding cannot explain — the registries are mixed-vintage. (Against the measurement sigma this is only ~3.1 sigma; that weaker framing is recorded in the data block but is not the test.)

assertions.name: neutron_leg_favours_ratio_consistent_proton
assertions.source: Indicator (1 = the ratio-derived proton lands inside 1 sigma of the stored CODATA direct neutron while the stored proton falls outside it). m_p + m_e + Q_beta must reproduce that independently-stored neutron: the ratio-derived proton lands at 0.32 sigma, the stored proton misses by 2.96 sigma (9.3x worse). An independent observable therefore picks out the stored m_p as the stale member.

description: Internal triangulation of the over-determined CODATA registries (m_e, m_p/m_e, m_p) plus independent neutron and muon legs. Shows the corpus registries are mutually inconsistent at ~1.35 ppb — far outside their own quoted uncertainties — and that this inconsistency accounts for 100% of the m_p row's scored L2 error, which is therefore bookkeeping, not a theory residual. Audit-only: changes no prediction.
